target.title: fix(minimax): apply request policy to media generation requests
target.body:
## Summary
- MiniMax video, music, and image generation now pass `models.providers.<providerId>.request` into provider HTTP resolution instead of silently ignoring configured request overrides.
- MiniMax video follow-up requests now carry the same resolved request policy through status polling, file metadata retrieval, direct video downloads, and file-id video downloads.
- MiniMax music URL downloads now use the same guarded request policy as the initial music generation request.
- The guarded video/music follow-up requests preserve the existing provider poll/download retry semantics instead of turning transient failures into immediate user-visible failures.
- Removes the image caller-level hard-coded `allowPrivateNetwork: false` so configured request policy can control private-network access while the default remains deny-by-default when no request override is configured.
- collision check: searched `minimax request policy`, `minimax allowPrivateNetwork`, and `minimax video proxy`; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found for these MiniMax media generation paths.

## Verification
- `TMPDIR=/media/vdc/0668001470/tmp/openclaw-task-tmp node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/minimax/video-generation-provider.test.ts extensions/minimax/music-generation-provider.test.ts extensions/minimax/image-generation-provider.test.ts` - passed; `Test Files  3 passed (3)`, `Tests  31 passed (31)`.
- `TMPDIR=/media/vdc/0668001470/tmp/openclaw-task-tmp OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/minimax/video-generation-provider.ts extensions/minimax/video-generation-provider.test.ts extensions/minimax/music-generation-provider.ts extensions/minimax/music-generation-provider.test.ts extensions/minimax/image-generation-provider.ts extensions/minimax/image-generation-provider.test.ts extensions/minimax/provider-http.test-helpers.ts` - passed; exit 0.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo` - passed; exit 0.
- `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` - passed; exit 0.
- focused regression coverage now asserts the resolved MiniMax request policy reaches video status polling, file-id metadata retrieval, direct/file-id video downloads, and music URL downloads via guarded fetch calls.
- focused retry coverage now asserts transient video status polling and music URL download failures retry while the guarded request policy remains attached to each retry attempt.
- mutation check: temporarily removing the image `request:` parameter made `extensions/minimax/image-generation-provider.test.ts` fail because `resolveProviderHttpRequestConfig` no longer received the configured request object; restoring the patch returned the test to green.
- mutation check from the original commit: temporarily removing the video and music `request:` parameters made the focused Vitest fail with `expected undefined to deeply equal { allowPrivateNetwork: true, headers: ... }` in both portal media tests; restoring the patch returned the test to green.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: MiniMax video/music/image generation now honor configured provider request overrides such as custom headers and `allowPrivateNetwork` for the active provider id. The actual network-path proof below exercises video and music against a local MiniMax-compatible `node:http` endpoint; image is covered by a focused regression because MiniMax image generation intentionally uses a dedicated fixed regional endpoint rather than the text/media `baseUrl`.

Real environment tested: local Linux Node source checkout; actual exported MiniMax portal video and music provider builders; local `node:http` server; no third-party MiniMax network traffic; proxy env vars unset for the proof process.

Exact command run after this patch:

```text
env HTTP_PROXY= HTTPS_PROXY= http_proxy= https_proxy= ALL_PROXY= all_proxy= NO_PROXY= no_proxy= node --import tsx scratchpad/minimax-request-policy-proof.mts
```

The temporary proof script was not committed. It configured `models.providers.minimax-portal.request` with `allowPrivateNetwork: true` and `headers: { "X-MiniMax-Proof": "policy-applied" }`, then called the real MiniMax portal video and music providers against the local endpoint.

Observed output after fix:

```text
minimax-request-policy-proof
video_files=1
music_files=1
provider_paths=/v1/video_generation,/v1/query/video_generation?task_id=video-task,/v1/music_generation
proof_headers=policy-applied,policy-applied,policy-applied
auth_headers=Bearer ***,Bearer ***,Bearer ***
```

Evidence after fix: the local endpoint received configured request headers on the actual video submit request, video poll request, and music generation request, and both providers returned generated media. Additional focused regression coverage verifies that the follow-up legs ClawSweeper called out now receive guarded request options, including video status polling, file metadata retrieval, generated video download, and music URL download. Additional retry regression coverage verifies that guarded video polling and music URL downloads still use provider poll/download retry semantics. The image regression separately verifies the image provider passes the same sanitized request object to provider HTTP resolution and that the final image POST receives `allowPrivateNetwork: true` plus the configured header.

target.title: fix(ui): active split pane indicator renders as offset, non-parallel accent lines
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users focusing a pane in the web UI split view would see two accent "selection" lines that looked shifted against each other — one on the split toolbar and one on the pane below, starting at different x-offsets with different lengths, so the indicator read as a rendering glitch rather than a focus marker.

The mismatch is structural: the split toolbar is `position: fixed` with equal-width flex entries (one per pane, flattened across columns), while the panes below are laid out with per-column/pane weights and resizable dividers. Two paired horizontal accent lines drawn on those independent layers can never align, and dragging a divider makes the offset arbitrarily large.

## Why This Change Was Made

Instead of trying to align two lines that live on layers with independent geometry, each layer now marks focus with a self-contained shape: the active toolbar entry gets a subtle accent background tint (matching the app's existing active-tab idiom), and the active pane gets a 1px inset accent focus ring. Narrow mode shows only the active pane, so the ring is suppressed there. No markup, class-name, or behavior changes — CSS only.

## User Impact

The focused split pane is still clearly marked in both the toolbar and the content area, but the indicator now looks intentional at any pane size — no more skewed, non-parallel accent lines after opening or resizing splits.

## Evidence

Captured with the deterministic mock-gateway e2e harness (`ui/src/test-helpers/control-ui-e2e.ts`), left pane active.

Before (two offset accent lines; worse after dragging the divider):

![before default](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/split-pane-active-indicator/before-top.png)
![before resized](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/split-pane-active-indicator/before-resized-top.png)

After (toolbar tint + pane focus ring; stable under resize):

![after default](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/split-pane-active-indicator/after-top.png)
![after resized](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/split-pane-active-indicator/after-resized-top.png)

- `oxfmt --check` clean on the touched file.
- Codex autoreview (branch vs `origin/main`): clean, no actionable findings.
- Existing coverage unaffected: `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-page.test.ts` and `ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.e2e.test.ts` assert the `--active` class wiring, which is unchanged.
